key_insight: A humanoid controller can often solve new tasks by reusing skills it already has, if those skills are exposed through a planning-to-control interface expressive enough to represent contact-rich, multi-stage behaviors. The paper shows that the robot can improve at test time by evolving its own reward programs, without retraining the policy.
problem_solved: This paper tackles the challenge of making humanoid robots handle unseen loco-manipulation tasks at test time—tasks they were never explicitly trained for—while avoiding costly retraining and preserving learned improvements.
method: Use test-time evolution to adapt reward programs rather than retraining the controller.
Let the robot attempt the task, evaluate its own behavior, and iteratively improve the reward specification based on those attempts.
Exploit a broad pre-trained controller and an expressive interface between planning and control to unlock existing capabilities for contact-rich, multi-stage interaction.
impact: This approach offers a practical path for deploying humanoid robots in new environments and tasks with less data, less retraining, and faster adaptation. For practitioners, it suggests a way to turn general-purpose controllers into task-specific performers at test time.

paper_title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
paper_authors: Zhuo Lin, Sirui Xu, Liuyu Bian, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui
